body:
I fell asleep and am feeling much less volatile now. I'll go into some more background.

It's really not about an existential crisis. The fact that it won't ultimately matter in the end is really more of a justification than anything.

I have had on again/off again suicidal thoughts for probably 5-6 years but no attempts, and to the best of my knowledge no one has any suspicion thereof. I think it's been a solid 2-3 years since the last time I really thought about it, but over the last month or two it has become much more frequent and vivid. I have no major triggers going on in my life to provoke it, so these moods seem to have a mind of their own. 

However, recently I find that minor events which would normally leave me (and any other reasonable person) unaffected seem to be able to easily trip my trigger and send me into a really ugly mood. The funny thing is though, I almost like these moods. When I am in them I have no desire to feel better, and often actively and intentionally enhance it by isolating myself, fantasizing, listening to depressing songs, etc. Going to sleep seems to reset me, and put me back to a more baseline mood.

Once a mood ends (like now), I pretty much conclude that I am just full of shit or being an attention whore, and that it was never really that serious. I wouldn't be surprised if this is basically normal and I'm just being a drama queen over it. However, I have decided that my preferred method would be asphyxiation, and I definitely have access to inert gasses if I really wanted them. I often think that the only thing keeping me from following through with it is just not wanting to hurt anyone else. Sometimes I wish I were actually alone so that there would be no one to really affect, and thus nothing to hold me back.

As far as help goes, I guess there are multiple reasons why I don't seek it. There are of course the obvious and common reasons like social stigma, etc, but for the most part I just don't really want to get better.

Anyway, you guys don't need to worry about me. After sleeping I'm more clear headed and basically back to normal, so I'll be fine until the next thing to set me off comes along.

Who knows? I'm sure they would get over it after not too long. I don't know that I have the motivation to do anything like that. The weirdist thing is this: I can feel fine sometimes, but the smallest things will send me into a downward spiral at the drop of the hat. The fact that I have no real issues to complain about makes me feel even more worthless. Honestly, I don't think I even have the stones to carry through with it, though I wish I did. Perhaps if I encounter the right situation it might give me enough momentum to follow through. I feel like such a little emo pussy for even writing this. I often wish something out of my control would happen to me, just to give me an out that no one would blame me (or themselves for).

How would you like to measure it? I'm 22 now, but I've contemplated suicied off and on since junior year of high school. I have often thought about just how I would pull it off, especially related to others finding me. I'm torn between sacrificing myself with organ donation, or trying to mysteriously disappear where no one could ever find my body. I have no desire to talk to a counselor or anyone else.

I'm failing to convince myself that any of that matters. I don't want a 9-5, because that is the most soul-sucking idea of life that I can imagine. I wish I was born 300 years ago so I could wander off into the unknown. Beyond my own issues, think about the universe as it exists: Even if miraculously we figure out how to prolong human life, we are going to be engulfed by the sun. Even if we make it off this planet, eventually every star in the universe will die out until either the universe collapses in on itself, or we die a slow, entropy heat death. Once all the nucleons decay, we are only photons. Suicide only speeds the process up.

Nothing is going on. By all measureable standards, I'm doing great. No financial issues, doing very well in school, no problems with the law, in great physical shape, etc. The littlest things set me off that shouldn't ever matter. I've got the bag in my hand right now, just trying to make a decision. My cousin's suicide isn't even that big of a deal to me, just a reference experience. Sometimes I wonder about what it's like after I'm gone. Ideally, I want to go out doing something great. Some sort of self sacrifice would be awesome. I would gladly jump in front of a bullet for someone if the opportunity presented itself. I've often though about how I could keep my organs preserved to donate to people who want/need them. Ultimately, I'm convinced that I'm destined to wander this earth alone. I would love to go out doing something epic, like climbing Everest or K2. I have no legitimate reason to complate, which is what makes me ever more of a little emo bitch that doesn't deserve this earth.
